evidence_text: All entities are exposed to some form of market risk. Many financial institutions and corporate businesses (entities) use derivative financial instruments to hedge their exposure to different risks

Many financial institutions and corporate businesses (entities) use derivative financial instruments to hedge their exposure to different risks...For many entities this would result in a significant amount of profit and loss volatility arising from the use of derivatives.
logical_form: if entities use derivatives, then it results in profit and loss volatility
mechanism: Using derivatives without hedge accounting leads to marking-to-market, which causes profit and loss volatility.

evidence_text: Accounting for derivative financial instruments under International Accounting Standards is covered by IAS39 (Financial Instrument: Recognition and Measurement). IAS39 requires that all derivatives are marked-to-market
logical_form: if IAS39 covers derivative accounting, then all derivatives are marked-to-market

evidence_text: IAS39 requires that all derivatives are marked-to-market with changes in the mark-to-market being taken to the profit and loss account. For many entities this would result in a significant amount of profit and loss volatility arising from the use of derivatives.
logical_form: if derivatives are marked-to-market, then it results in profit and loss volatility
mechanism: Marking-to-market derivatives directly impacts the profit and loss account, leading to volatility.

evidence_text: IAS39 requires that all derivatives are marked-to-market with changes in the mark-to-market being taken to the profit and loss account. An entity can mitigate the profit and loss effect arising from derivatives used for hedging, through an optional part of IAS39 relating to hedge accounting.
logical_form: if derivatives are marked-to-market, then entities need hedge accounting to mitigate profit and loss effect
mechanism: The requirement to mark-to-market creates a need for hedge accounting to manage the resulting profit and loss volatility.

evidence_text: An entity can mitigate the profit and loss effect arising from derivatives used for hedging, through an optional part of IAS39 relating to hedge accounting. Not all hedges are designated for special accounting treatment.
logical_form: if hedge accounting is optional, then not all hedges are designated for special accounting treatment

evidence_text: A specific type of hedging transaction that entities can engage in aims to manage foreign currency exposure. These hedges are undertaken for the economic aim of reducing potential loss from fluctuations in foreign exchange rates.
logical_form: if entities engage in hedging transaction, then it aims to manage foreign currency exposure
mechanism: Hedging transactions are specifically designed to reduce potential losses from foreign exchange rate fluctuations.

evidence_text: Accounting standards enable hedge accounting for three different designated forex hedges. A cash flow hedge may be designated for a highly probable forecasted transaction
Accounting standards enable hedge accounting for three different designated forex hedges. A fair value hedge may be designated for a firm commitment
Accounting standards enable hedge accounting for three different designated forex hedges. A net investment hedge may be designated for the net investment in a foreign operation.
